I am 78 years old, and my bones know this land better than any book. I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. My son and his wife work in the county town, so it is mainly me and my wife who tend the fields, with our son coming back for the busy harvest and planting days. We cannot afford to waste energy or money on things that do not pay back.

**Wheat (winter crop):** I will plant the same improved wheat variety my neighbors and I have used for years — it is reliable, and I save my own seed from the best heads. I will give the wheat about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, because too much makes it lodge and too little leaves it thin. I add some phosphorus and potassium because the soil here needs it after so many years of wheat-maize, but I do not go overboard — about 5 kg each per mu. I will irrigate four times: once before winter to help it establish, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at flowering. The well water is there, but pumping costs money, so I watch the sky and cut one if it rains well. Two pesticide sprays — one for aphids and powdery mildew in spring, and another if I see rust. I will rotary till before planting to bury the maize stubble and break the surface crust. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the spring is kind.

**Maize (summer crop):** Time is everything after wheat harvest. I will buy hybrid maize seed from the supply shop — the same type everyone plants, the one with the big ears. No time for deep ploughing; I will run the rotary tiller quickly or even direct-seed if the wheat stubble is not too thick. Nitrogen at 15 kg per mu, a little phosphorus, and about 4 kg potassium. Two irrigations: one right after emergence if the June heat is fierce, and one at the big flare stage. Sometimes a third at grain filling if the August drought hits hard. Two pesticide applications: one at the seedling stage for armyworm and corn borer, and another at ear stage if the borers come back. I expect around 520 kg per mu in a normal year.

I do not chase new fads. I use what works, what my hands have proven year after year. My goal is to feed my household and have a little grain left to sell for cash. I am too old to gamble on strange varieties or reckless spending.
